s1.syndrome_frame: Acute right lower quadrant abdominal pain with fever and elevated inflammatory markers
salient_findings: Pain in the right lower quadrant without peritoneal signs
Abdominal CT scan showing a swollen and thickened tubular structure with a pericecal collection
key_facts: 58-year-old man
24-hour history of right iliac fossa pain
Nausea and diarrhea
History of laparoscopic appendectomy 8 months earlier
Febrile
Hemodynamic and respiratory parameters stable
Pain in the right lower quadrant without peritoneal signs
White-blood-cell count of 25,000 cells/mm3 with 85% neutrophils
C-reactive protein level of 180 mg/dL
Abdominal CT scan showed a swollen and thickened tubular structure measuring 36 × 27 mm at the cecal pole
25-mm pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips

shortlist.label: Stump appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of laparoscopic appendectomy and CT findings of a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole with a pericecal collection

shortlist.label: Inflamed residual appendiceal stump
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to stump appendicitis, with CT demonstrating a remaining stump and abscess

shortlist.label: Cecal diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Right lower quadrant pain and elevated inflammatory markers, with CT findings consistent with diverticulitis

shortlist.label: Pericecal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: CT findings of a 25-mm pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips, consistent with an abscess

shortlist.label: Duplicated appendix
shortlist.why_kept: Rare anatomic anomaly that can cause post-appendectomy appendicitis, with symptoms and CT findings consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of laparoscopic appendectomy and the presence of a swollen and thickened tubular structure at the cecal pole with a pericecal collection adjacent to surgical clips on the CT scan support this diagnosis, as it suggests inflammation of the appendiceal stump.

rejected.label: Inflamed residual appendiceal stump
rejected.why: This is essentially the same condition as stump appendicitis, and the CT findings support stump appendicitis as the more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cecal diverticulitis
rejected.why: While cecal diverticulitis could present with similar right-lower-quadrant pain, the presence of surgical clips and the specific location of the swollen structure at the cecal pole suggest a complication related to the previous appendectomy rather than diverticulitis.

rejected.label: Pericecal abscess
rejected.why: The patient does have a pericecal collection, but this is likely a consequence of the stump appendicitis rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Duplicated appendix
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the case to support the rare diagnosis of a duplicated appendix, making stump appendicitis a more likely explanation for the patient's symptoms and findings.
